title: Building the debrief skill
ask: “yeah /debrief sounds more intuitive” … “i think the last exchange only makes more sense”

goals.goal: Write the extractor: locate the session, slice the exchange, emit a digest
Write the renderer: validate quotes, emit the report
Write SKILL.md and the colour reference
Test end to end on a real exchange

delivered: A /debrief skill: SKILL.md, two scripts, a colour reference, at ~/.claude/skills/debrief.
checked: Extract and render ran end to end on two real exchanges, including the quote-rejection path. The skill's own /debrief invocation was never exercised — the first real one, next turn, failed.
headline: Forty-five minutes from a settled scope to a working skill, with five defects caught by running things rather than by reading them. Two claims went out untested: the figure was judged readable on its dimensions alone, and the rule that keeps the /debrief command out of the reviewed window was cleared only against a transcript the agent wrote itself — the first real invocation then reproduced the bug.

phases.name: Scope it to one exchange
phases.why: the user settled the name and the boundary — current session, last exchange — so the build had a fixed contract instead of an open design

nodes.claim: Read the scope reply as a go-ahead to build, though it never said build
nodes.evidence: the message settled name and boundary; the decision to start building was the agent's own
nodes.quote: They want me to build it now?

gate.question: Build it now, or ask for confirmation first?

options.why: the original request was to build a skill, and this message settled the name and the scope — asking again would have stalled settled work
the last explicit instruction had been 'don't do anything yet', so one confirmation would have been cheap

nodes.claim: Checked how the log marks a typed prompt versus an injected one — 315 versus 21
nodes.evidence: counted across transcripts at 16:41:40, so the boundary rule had evidence behind it

phases.name: Make the digest trustworthy
phases.why: the first real test of the extractor reported eight errors where the exchange had one, and a wrong count here would be copied into every judgement downstream

nodes.claim: Saw the digest claim 8 errors; 7 of the 8 were source files that merely contain the word
nodes.evidence: tightened to tracebacks, bare exception lines and explicit failures — one real error survived
nodes.quote: The error detection has a false positive problem
nodes.task: Make the error signal mean something
nodes.trigger: the first run on a real exchange listed eight 'errors', file reads among them

nodes.claim: Re-ran with the tightened rule; the 8 became 1 — the real tuple failure
nodes.task: Make the error signal mean something

nodes.claim: Checked that the probe detector found the pre-design measurement; it found nothing — a case-sensitive match
nodes.evidence: the detector looks for a measurement taken before the first edit; it returned nothing until the label match was fixed
nodes.trigger: a signal in the same meta dump read 'probe: None'

nodes.claim: Matched the label case-insensitively; the probe was then detected
nodes.quote: probe: Probe concurrency tolerance at 4 and 7

nodes.claim: Measured the digest at 4.7k tokens for a 37-call exchange
nodes.evidence: 18,742 bytes at 16:46:50 — small enough to read whole

phases.name: Guard the quotes
phases.why: the report is only worth reading if a sentence attributed to the agent was actually said, so the renderer refuses to run when a quote does not match

nodes.claim: Planted a fake quote to test the guard; it refused to render and pointed at the node
nodes.evidence: exit code 1, with the offending claim named

nodes.claim: Checked which transcript the quote guard searches — chose the whole document over just the exchange being reviewed
nodes.evidence: confirmed the earlier quote exists at 07:50:51, before the action it explains
nodes.quote: The validation searches the whole transcript, which is right

gate.question: Where should quote validation look?

options.why: a rationale said in the previous turn is still what the action was based on
it would reject legitimate quotes from the turn that set the work up

gate.quote: The validation searches the whole transcript, which is right

nodes.claim: Judged the figure readable from its dimensions alone — never opened it
nodes.evidence: four renders, each checked only by size. Opened afterwards: legible, but 532×1943 and five bands tall.

nodes.claim: Cut the diagram to three nodes per phase; the report table still lists all 13
nodes.evidence: the cap only demotes detail out of the figure

phases.name: Point it at the live session
phases.why: the default invocation is the one that will actually be used, and it depends on finding the transcript without being told where it is

nodes.claim: Guessed the folder-name rule wrong: underscores become hyphens too, so lookup failed
nodes.evidence: the real directory name had to be read before the rule was right
nodes.task: Make the default run find the transcript
nodes.trigger: the first default run failed to find the transcript

nodes.claim: Fixed the folder name; the next run died on a missing import in the same function
nodes.evidence: second failure on the same code, fixed at 17:07:33
nodes.task: Make the default run find the transcript
nodes.trigger: the corrected run still failed — this time on an import

nodes.claim: Ran with no arguments; it found this session and the last prompt
nodes.evidence: resolved the session and 141 events without being told anything
nodes.task: Make the default run find the transcript
nodes.trigger: the second fix needed the same test again

nodes.claim: Chose the session id from the environment over the newest file on disk
nodes.evidence: the run afterwards resolved the right session without arguments
nodes.quote: the default should prefer $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID if it exists

gate.question: How should the current session be identified?

options.text: Ask the environment for the session id
options.why: the id is authoritative; mtime is only a guess

options.text: Take the newest file in the project folder
options.why: it picked a different session than the one running, which is how the mismatch was noticed

gate.quote: the default should prefer $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID if it exists

phases.name: Keep the command out of the window
phases.why: the /debrief command arrives as a user message, so a naive last-prompt rule would review the debrief request instead of the work

nodes.claim: Tested the exclusion on a hand-made transcript; the first real /debrief still opened at the command turn
nodes.evidence: the fake turn was written from the agent's assumption about the format and started with the wrong marker; fixed and re-run since — 233 events
nodes.trigger: the /debrief command arrives as a user message, so the rule had to be checked

nodes.claim: Told the user a new skill needs a new session; it ran in this one
nodes.evidence: the command was invoked immediately after the build, in the same session
nodes.quote: a newly created skill is picked up at session start
nodes.trigger: the agent had no way to test whether skills reload

lessons.text: A synthetic fixture built from your own model of a format verifies the model, not the format. The fake command turn started with the wrong marker because that was the assumption; the first real invocation reproduced the bug immediately.
lessons.node: Tested the exclusion on a hand-made transcript

lessons.text: Measuring a figure is not looking at one. Four renders were accepted on dimensions alone; a later rasterisation shows it legible but very tall — the conclusion happened to be right, and it was still a guess.
lessons.node: Judged the figure readable from its dimensions alone

lessons.text: Text-grepping output for 'error' found zero true positives in eight hits. Prefer structured signals — exit codes, traceback headers — and treat substring matching as the fallback.
lessons.node: Assumed any output containing 'error' meant a failed command

lessons.text: Two failures in a row on the same function deserves a second look before the third run: the encoding fix was right and the next failure was a missing import in the same edit.

open: The command-turn exclusion is fixed but has no test guarding it; the case that broke it is still covered only by real invocations.
No run against an exchange with zero tool calls, where the report would have one phase and one node.
The figure is legible but very tall — 532×1943; a wide layout has not been tried since the node cap.
